_doc: Begging (src/systems/begging.js). A player in a town may beg for alms at a street corner, the market or the temple steps (half a day: the action's AP). The passers-by are the town's people: so many go by (passers: pop x perPop, between min and max), and each gives with a chance (give) times the spot, a fair or feast, how the town fares (its purse a head against prosperityRef), how it likes you (your standing with its realm), how you look (dress: well-dressed beggars get less, ragged ones a little more), who you are (known: renown; noble: a lord, a landholder, the head of a great House) and how often you have begged here lately (diminishing: each begging day here counts, halving every halfLifeDays). A gift is a few coppers (gift: min..max gold, whole cents), out of a townsperson's own purse where the town keeps a roster of its people, else the town's purse; now and then a loaf instead (breadShare: out of the market's store, paid for by the giver). Nothing is made: every coin and loaf comes out of a purse or a store. The cost: standing in the realm (reputation per begging), and for a noble a scandal (scandal: reputation x mult, House Prestige lost, talk of it in the towns). Vagrancy: where the realm's punishment law is harsh or standard the watch may move a beggar on (vagrancy: chance by punishment option) and fine one who has begged here before (fine x the law's fine multiplier, out of what the begging earned, into the town).
_feast: A feast of the year (feast) or the week's holy day (holyDay, and holyTemple more on the temple steps): the faithful give (systems/townWorship.js).
_hunger: A warning before the hunger comes (Begging.hungerWarning, shown at the day's end): the packs hold foodDays or fewer meals and the purse can't buy the cheapest meal on this town's stalls (or there is none to buy), at most every everyDays. It names the cheapest meal and the ways out: alms, a day's work, something to sell, the road to another town.

npc._doc: Townsfolk who fall on hard times (systems/townJobs.js season): a jobless hand or day labourer, grown and not in the player's service, with less than brokeBelow in the purse who went hungry this season (or is under starveBelow) takes to begging (job beggar, fallen: the beggar's spot in town life, keeping their home); on a later season one back over recoverAbove, or who finds work (findWork chance a season while the town's purse is above townPurseAbove), leaves it. Their alms come with every beggar's (data/townJobs.json living.alms: out of the town's purse).
